identity.name: Unusual exec Into a Kubernetes Pod + Unusual Service-Account API Call (SIM-CDR-025)
identity.summary: A compromised in-cluster identity opens an interactive exec session into a running pod, then the pod's service account issues an RBAC-write API call it has never made in baseline. The k8s_audit_emitter streams shape-true audit.k8s.io/v1 records into the kubernetes_audit_logs data source so two XSIAM behavioral-ML (ABIOC) alerts fire: unusual pod exec, and an unusual service-account API call.
identity.description: Post-compromise Kubernetes tradecraft: an attacker who has landed in the cluster (leaked SA token, exposed dashboard, or a compromised sidecar) runs `kubectl exec` to get an interactive shell inside a running workload pod (Container Administration Command, T1609), then rides the pod's mounted service-account token to perform an API operation the account never performs in normal operation — creating a ClusterRoleBinding to escalate (Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts, T1078.004). Both actions land in the Kubernetes API-server audit log. Cortex XSIAM's Kubernetes-audit analytics learn a per-principal baseline of who execs into which pods and which verbs/resources each service account touches; a deviation raises the ABIOC alerts 'Unusual exec into a Kubernetes Pod' and 'A Kubernetes service account executed an unusual API call'. This card drives the k8s_audit_emitter EAL plugin (event_pattern pod_exec then unusual_sa_api_call) to emit the exact records that exercise those detections without touching a real cluster or issuing any real API call.

prerequisites.description: Kubernetes API-server audit logging is enabled at RequestResponse level and forwarded into the XSIAM kubernetes_audit_logs data source (Broker VM / HTTP collector).
The operator-supplied HTTP log collector is reachable and on the campaign target_allowlist.

payload.code:
# Drive the k8s_audit_emitter EAL plugin to stream shape-true Kubernetes
# API-server audit records into the operator's collector. NO real cluster
# is touched; every record is a synthetic audit.k8s.io/v1 Event.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:?set COLLECTOR_URL to the operator HTTP collector}"
: "${COLLECTOR_HOST:?set COLLECTOR_HOST to the collector hostname}"
cat > /tmp/sim-cdr-025.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-CDR-025
name: "CDR — unusual pod exec + unusual SA API call"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - "${COLLECTOR_HOST}"
dry_run: false
steps:
  - step_id: exec
    plugin: k8s_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "${COLLECTOR_URL}"
      event_pattern: pod_exec
      iterations: 1
  - step_id: sa-api
    plugin: k8s_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "${COLLECTOR_URL}"
      event_pattern: unusual_sa_api_call
      iterations: 1
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/sim-cdr-025.yml --live

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator HTTP collector the shape-true kubernetes_audit_logs records POST to.

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_HOST
input_variables.description: Collector hostname added to the campaign target_allowlist for the authorise gate.

expected_artifacts.description: pods/exec create audit record (verb=create, subresource=exec, response 101) in kubernetes_audit_logs.
clusterrolebindings create audit record by a service-account principal (verb=create, response 201) in kubernetes_audit_logs.

cleanup.code: rm -f /tmp/sim-cdr-025.yml; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-025 cleanup complete (synthetic audit stream only; no cluster state changed).'

abiocs.name: Unusual exec into a Kubernetes Pod
abiocs.description: PANW-authored behavioral-ML detection over the Kubernetes API-server audit feed. It learns, per principal, the pods that identity normally execs into and raises when a create pods/exec subresource request deviates from that baseline (a principal execing into a pod it has never touched, or a service-account principal execing at all). Keyed on the kubernetes_audit_logs dataset.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs
| filter verb = "create" and objectRef_resource = "pods" and objectRef_subresource = "exec"
| comp count() as exec_events by user_username, objectRef_name, sourceIPs
| filter exec_events >= 1
| fields user_username, objectRef_name, sourceIPs, exec_events
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-principal exec baseline: which user/service-account normally opens pods/exec into which pod (objectRef.name) from which sourceIP. The deviation anchors to the pod's container image and the acting identity's exec history.

abiocs.name: A Kubernetes service account executed an unusual API call
abiocs.description: PANW-authored behavioral-ML detection over the Kubernetes API-server audit feed. It learns, per service account, the verb+resource pairs that account exercises in baseline and raises when a service-account principal issues an out-of-profile RBAC-write (creating a ClusterRoleBinding / ClusterRole it never touches). Keyed on the kubernetes_audit_logs dataset.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs
| filter user_username contains "system:serviceaccount:"
| filter verb in ("create", "update", "patch") and objectRef_resource in ("clusterrolebindings", "rolebindings", "clusterroles")
| comp count() as rbac_writes by user_username, verb, objectRef_resource, objectRef_name
| filter rbac_writes >= 1
| fields user_username, verb, objectRef_resource, objectRef_name, rbac_writes
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-service-account API baseline: the verb+resource pairs (user.username -> verb/objectRef.resource) the account exercises normally. The deviation anchors to the compromised service account identity and the RBAC-write resource it has no baseline for.

xql_queries.name: SIM-CDR-025 Kubernetes Audit Emission Validation
xql_queries.query:
dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter cortexsim_run_id != null
| filter pod_exec_marker = true or unusual_sa_api_call_marker = true
| comp count() as audit_records by user_username, verb, objectRef_resource, objectRef_subresource
| filter audit_records >= 1
| fields user_username, verb, objectRef_resource, objectRef_subresource, audit_records

correlation_rules.name: SIM-CDR-025 Exec Then Unusual SA API Correlation
correlation_rules.logic: Fires when abioc `Unusual exec into a Kubernetes Pod` and abioc `A Kubernetes service account executed an unusual API call` both observe activity attributable to the same service-account principal (user.username) within a 15-minute window, stitching the interactive-exec foothold and the follow-on RBAC-write escalation into one Kubernetes intrusion incident.

use_cases.name: Kubernetes audit — unusual pod exec and service-account API abuse
use_cases.description: Validate that Cortex XSIAM's Kubernetes-audit behavioral analytics detect an interactive exec into a running pod and a follow-on out-of-baseline service-account RBAC-write, and stitch them into one incident.

test_cases.objective: An interactive create pods/exec by an out-of-baseline principal raises the unusual-pod-exec ABIOC.
preconditions: Kubernetes audit logging forwarded into kubernetes_audit_logs.
steps: Run the k8s_audit_emitter with event_pattern pod_exec.
Observe the ABIOC 'Unusual exec into a Kubernetes Pod' fire.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Unusual exec into a Kubernetes Pod` fires within the run window.

test_cases.objective: A service-account RBAC-write it never performs in baseline raises the unusual-SA-API-call ABIOC and the correlation stitches both alerts.
preconditions: The unusual-pod-exec ABIOC has already fired for the same run.
steps: Run the k8s_audit_emitter with event_pattern unusual_sa_api_call.
Observe the second ABIOC and correlation CR-CDR-0025 fire.
success_criteria: ABIOC `A Kubernetes service account executed an unusual API call` fires.
Correlation `CR-CDR-0025` raises one incident stitching both ABIOCs.

preventive_controls: Restrict pods/exec via RBAC — grant the create pods/exec permission only to break-glass admin roles, never to workload service accounts.
Disable automatic service-account token mounting (automountServiceAccountToken: false) on workload pods that do not call the Kubernetes API.
Scope service-account RBAC to least privilege; deny cluster-scoped RBAC-write (clusterrolebindings/clusterroles) to namespaced workload identities.
detection_engineering: Enable API-server audit at RequestResponse level for the pods/exec subresource and for rbac.authorization.k8s.io write verbs, and forward to the kubernetes_audit_logs dataset.
Baseline, per principal, which identities exec into which pods and which verb+resource pairs each service account exercises; alert on first-seen deviations.
Correlate an interactive exec foothold with a follow-on service-account RBAC-write attributable to the same principal within a short window.
